newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets new rules for share issues.
newsitem.headline: China sets new rules for share issues.

text.p: China has promulgated a set of new rules governing share issues ordering local governments to give priority to firms operating in basic sectors of the economy, the Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.
The rules, issued by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the nation's top securities watchdog, said that finance and real estate firms must not issue shares for the time being.
Firms engaged in agriculture, energy, transportation, telecommunications and raw materials will be given priority, it said.

From now on, approval for share issues will be based on an analysis of a company's post-tax profits in the previous three years instead of on its prediction of future profits as in the past, the rules said.

A newly-listed company which declares annual net profits 10 to 20 percent lower than predicted in its share issue prospectus must explain the reason for the decrease and publicly apologise to investors, the rules said.
A company which posts profits more than 20 percent below the predicted level will be investigated, the rules said.
Accountants who fail to strictly audit a newly-listed company's profit forecast, resulting in a big shortfall against actual results will be punished, the rules said but gave no further details.
Local governments must make detailed feasibility studies of projects which a company proposes to develop using share issue proceeds, the rules said.
Underwriters also have a responsibility to train company officials on the procedures for establishing a listed firm, they added.
